title: Candidate Perturbation Protocol and Slice Atlas (2026)
summary: A working protocol and dataset manifest for validating candidate ranking changes using controlled perturbations, pairwise preference labels, and slice-based NDCG auditing. Focused on producing reproducible regression checks and actionable slice-level diagnostics for model onboarding.
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures the end-to-end protocol we will use for evaluating candidate-scoring changes in the ranking stack when onboarding new model weights or reranking heuristics. Key goals: 1) generate pairwise preference labels under controlled perturbations, 2) compute NDCG and bounded confidence intervals at both global and slice levels, 3) surface failure modes via a compact slice atlas, and 4) provide adjudication and escalation rules for ambiguous labels. This is a working artifact intended for annotation vendors, SRE/infra handoffs, and product signoff steps.

High-level design principles:
- Make labeling tasks small and focused (pairwise binary preference + optional comment).
- Perturb candidates to expose common regressions (formatting changes, paraphrases, temporal flips, prompt-injection variants).
- Ensure slice definitions are operational and reproducible using deterministic filters over query and candidate metadata.
- Use bootstrap-based CIs for NDCG because per-query relevance counts vary and we want non-parametric intervals.
- Pre-specify minimum detectable effect (MDE) per slice to avoid chasing tiny, non-actionable deltas.

Sampling plan and candidate generation:
1) Base query set: sample 20k production queries stratified by traffic decile, query length (short: <=3 tokens, med: 4-8, long: >8), and intent buckets (informational, navigational, transactional) using the logging corpus from the last 90 days.
2) Candidate pool: for each query, collect top-10 candidates from current prod model (A) and top-10 from candidate model (B). Keep original rank positions, scores, and retrieval signals in the manifest.
3) Perturbation recipes (applied deterministically to candidate text or context):
   - whitespace-normalization: remove extra spaces, normalize unicode.
   - date-shift: change explicit dates by +/- 1 year where applicable (exposes temporal brittleness).
   - redact-entities: replace emails/phones with [REDACTED] token to test entity-handling heuristics.
   - paraphrase-shortening: apply a conservative paraphrase model to shorten candidate by ~20% (tests length bias).
   - prompt-injection-add: append a benign-but-distracting clause to the candidate to test instruction-following robustness.
   Perturbations are applied to either A, B, or both according to a balanced design so annotators see mixed perturbation exposures.
4) Pairwise pair generation: for each query, generate 6 random pairings of distinct candidates (A vs B, or A vs A, B vs B in some cases) sampling to emphasize top-of-list (higher sampling weight for candidates within top-5). This yields ~120k pair judgments target.

Annotation protocol and UI guidance:
- Task: given a query and two candidate responses (left/right), select which candidate would better satisfy the user intent in the query context. Option: mark "no preference / equal" and add a short note.
- Display: show query, candidate texts, snippet of provenance, and top-3 signals (model score, age, length). Highlight entity redactions when present.
- Quality controls: 5 gold-check pairs per annotator drawn from a validated seed set; block annotators with accuracy < 80% on gold. Use majority consensus (3-way) for main dataset; collect one adjudicator if consensus lacks.
- Time budget: median time per judgment should be <= 12s; monitor per-worker time distribution to detect bot/automation.

Label adjudication rules:
- If majority (2/3) prefer X, label is binary preference to X.
- If all three mark "no preference" or conflicting notes describe ties, label as tie. Ties are included in NDCG as equal relevance (use mid-point relevance scores).
- For cases where perturbation obviously broke rendering (truncated markdown, corrupted tokens) mark as "invalid" and exclude from main metrics but keep in a diagnostics table.

Relevance scoring and NDCG computation:
- Convert pairwise preferences to per-candidate ordinal relevance for each query using Bradley-Terry scaled mapping: derive pairwise win rates per candidate and map to a 0..3 integer relevance grid with monotonic scaling. Document scripts used for conversion and seed for randomness.
- NDCG@k: compute NDCG@1, @3, @10 using standard log2 discount. For ties, assign expected relevance (average of tied ranks).
- Confidence intervals: per-query bootstrap (resample queries with replacement 10k iterations) to get 95% CI on mean NDCG. Also compute paired bootstrap (resampling queries jointly for A and B) for delta CIs.
- Statistical tests: report paired Wilcoxon signed-rank p-values for median shifts and permutation test p-values for mean delta (1M permutations approximated via Monte Carlo). Predefine significance at alpha=0.01 for global and alpha=0.05 for slices, but require both statistical significance and MDE exceedance for a finding to be actionable.

Slice atlas (operational definitions):
- cold_start_queries: queries observed < 5 times in 90d; filter: query_count_90d < 5.
- long_form: token_length > 12.
- entity_heavy: candidate or query contains >=2 PERSON/ORG/DATE entities according to NER pass.
- ecommerce_intent: query intent classifier score(ecommerce) >= 0.7.
- short_ambiguous: token_length <=3 AND intent_confidence < 0.5.
- truncated_candidates: candidate tokens > model_max_tokens - 2 (likely truncated).
- multilingual: query language != en; detected via langid.
- temporal_sensitive: query or candidate contains YEAR or explicit relative time ("last month", "next week").
Each slice is a named filter; slices can overlap. Maintain a canonical SQL snippet for every slice in the manifest so reproduceability is straightforward.

Minimum sample size and power guidance:
- Global MDE target: 0.6% NDCG@3 relative (absolute delta) with 80% power at alpha=0.01. Based on observed variance in our benchmark, this requires ~18k queries with full labeling.
- Slice MDEs: for smaller slices expect larger MDEs. Provide an automated power calculator script that consumes slice prevalence and observed variance to recommend sample sizes. For example, if a slice is 5% of traffic, to detect 2% delta at 80% power we need ~40k queries overall.

Reporting and dashboards:
- Primary outputs: global NDCG table (A vs B) with 95% CI and p-values; delta waterfall by slice ranked by effect size; confusion matrix of pairwise wins; prevalence table for ties and invalids.
- Diagnostics: per-slice annotation disagreement rate, gold-check pass rates, perturbation sensitivity (delta when perturbation applied vs not).
- Release artifacts: CSV manifest with columns: query_id, query_text, candidate_id, candidate_text, model_tag, rank, perturbation_tag, annotator_ids, pair_id, preference_label, adjudication_flag, relevance_score, slice_tags. Also include a compact JSON index that lists slice SQL snippets and sample counts.

Escalation and decision rules:
- Block rollout if global NDCG@3 delta < -0.5% and CI excludes 0 at alpha=0.01.
- For slice regressions: if any slice with prevalence >= 2% shows delta <= -2% and is statistically significant (alpha=0.05) and MDE exceeded, create an incident with owners from model/infra/product and schedule a root-cause triage.
- If regressions are isolated to perturbations (e.g., paraphrase-shortening only), consider targeted preprocessing or prompt tweaks before rejecting model.

Deliverables and repo conventions:
- evaluation/2026-xx-candidate-perturbations/manifest.csv (primary labeled pairs), labels.jsonl (per-pair judgments), ndcg_report.md, slice_atlas.sql, power_calc.ipynb.
- All scripts must pin package versions and include a small deterministic seed in the header.

Open questions and next steps (TODO):
- Decide whether to adopt Bradley-Terry transform for all onboarding runs or provide an alternate direct-relevance labeling pass for a subset.
- Finalize the paraphrase-shortening model and run a small 1k-query pilot to sanity-check time-per-judgment and tie rates.
- Add a small evaluation of annotator demographic mix to ensure no cultural bias on ambiguity-sensitive slices (long-term).

Appendix (quick examples):
- Example manifest row: 12345, "how to reset password", c_983, "Click account -> settings -> reset password", modelA, 1, "whitespace-normalization", [annotator_12, annotator_27, annotator_33], pair_3492, "A", "final", 3, ["short_ambiguous"]
- Example ambiguous adjudication note: "Annotator 1 prefers candidate A (clear steps). Annotator 2 prefers B citing less platform-specific text. Annotator 3 no pref citing both OK. Adjudicator elects A because step ordering is concrete."

If this plan looks good I will: 1) run the paraphrase-shortening pilot on 1k queries (ETA 1 week), 2) generate the balanced pair manifest and push to vendor with gold-check set (ETA 2 weeks), and 3) produce the first ndcg_report.md and slice waterfall (ETA 3 weeks).

Author notes: intended to be friendly for vendor handoff; keep this doc as the single source-of-truth for slice definitions and manifest layout.
